Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.util

Class StackItemStorage

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.util.StackItemStorage
All Implemented Interfaces:
SlotAccess
public class StackItemStorage extends Object implements SlotAccess
A fixed-size, NBT-persisted SlotAccess implementation. It gives all three loaders the item-handler insert/extract semantics and NBT shape ({Items:[{Slot, ...stack}], SetAside:[...]}) used by the block entities.

A saved item tag that cannot be read, or whose slot is out of range or already taken, is set aside rather than dropped: it is kept verbatim under SetAside, saved back with the block, and retried on every load, so contents from a temporarily missing mod return when it does.

Subclasses override onContentsChanged(int), isItemValid(int, ItemStack), and getSlotLimit(int) to specialize notification, admission, and capacity.

    • insertItem

      @Nonnull public net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack insertItem(int slot, @Nonnull net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, boolean simulate)
      Description copied from interface: SlotAccess
      Inserts as much of stack into slot as SlotAccess.isItemValid(int, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack) and SlotAccess.getSlotLimit(int) allow. Returns the remainder that was not accepted — ItemStack.EMPTY if all of it was — and never mutates stack itself. When simulate is true, the slot is left unchanged and only the would-be remainder is computed.
      Specified by:
      insertItem in interface SlotAccess

    • deserializeNBT

      public StackItemStorage.LoadResult deserializeNBT(net.minecraft.core.HolderLookup.Provider registries, net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag nbt)
      Loads slot contents from NBT, setting aside every item tag that cannot be placed. The tag must already be in the running game's format. Ordinary entries take precedence over retries; loading bypasses admission and does not call contents-change hooks. The caller reports returned retention counts once it knows the world location.
